name: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
oneLiner: The VPC itself is free. Everything you get billed for is something you attached to it.
trap: People hunt for a VPC line item and find nothing. The real cost is NAT gateways, interface endpoints, public IPv4 hours and cross-AZ transfer, each billed separately.

name: NAT Gateway
oneLiner: Charged per hour just for existing, plus a per-GB fee on every byte it touches.
trap: The per-GB data processing fee is direction-agnostic - downloads cost exactly what uploads do. 'Inbound is free' does not apply here, and it stacks on top of normal data transfer out.

name: Internet Gateway
oneLiner: The gateway is free; you only pay for the bytes that leave through it.
trap: There is no internet gateway line item - egress lands on EC2 DataTransfer-Out-Bytes. Inbound genuinely is free here, unlike NAT gateway processing. Egress-only IGW is free too.

name: AWS Transit Gateway
oneLiner: Hourly per attachment, then again per GB for traffic sent into the gateway.
trap: Every attachment bills hourly at zero traffic. Processing is direction-agnostic and charged to the sender, but traffic arriving from a peering attachment is not processed-charged again.

name: AWS PrivateLink Interface VPC Endpoint
oneLiner: Billed per hour per AZ per endpoint, plus per GB processed - the AZ count is what bites.
trap: Hourly billing runs per AZ even while the endpoint is pending or rejected, and the per-GB processing fee applies regardless of the traffic's source or destination - inbound is not free.

name: Gateway VPC Endpoint (S3, DynamoDB)
oneLiner: Genuinely free - no hourly fee, no per-GB fee, for S3 and DynamoDB only.
trap: Do not confuse with interface endpoints for the same services: those charge hourly AND per GB. Gateway endpoints are route-table based and cannot be reached over peering, VPN or Direct Connect.

name: Amazon VPC Peering
oneLiner: The peering connection costs nothing; only bytes crossing an AZ or Region boundary do.
trap: Same-AZ peering traffic is free, but cross-AZ is metered on BOTH resources - you see two line items for the same GB. Cross-Region charges the sending side; the receiving side is free.

name: Application Load Balancer (ALB)
oneLiner: An hourly fee plus LCUs, where an LCU is whichever of four dimensions runs hottest.
trap: LCU is the MAX of new connections, active connections, processed bytes and rule evaluations - not the sum. A chatty low-byte API can bill entirely on connections, never on traffic.

name: Network Load Balancer (NLB)
oneLiner: Hourly fee plus NLCUs; long-lived TCP flows cost more than the byte count suggests.
trap: NLCU is the MAX of new flows, active flows and processed bytes. Peak concurrent flows are sampled every minute, so idle-but-open connections bill even with near-zero traffic.

name: Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
oneLiner: Hourly per AZ plus GLCUs - and the endpoints sitting in front of it bill separately.
trap: Gateway Load Balancer Endpoints are a distinct PrivateLink-style charge with their own hourly and per-GB fees. Budgeting only the GWLB itself misses a large slice of the bill.

name: Amazon CloudFront
oneLiner: Per GB out to viewers and per request - plus per GB going back the other way to your origin.
trap: AWS-origin to edge is free, but edge back to origin (POST/PUT bodies, uploads) bills as DataTransfer-Out-OBytes. Invalidations past 1,000 paths a month also cost per path.

name: Amazon Route 53
oneLiner: Every DNS query is a billable request; hosted zones and Resolver ENIs bill by the clock.
trap: DNS queries really are a per-request charge. Alias records pointing at ELB/CloudFront/API Gateway and all private hosted zone queries are free, but Resolver endpoint ENIs bill hourly regardless.

name: AWS Global Accelerator
oneLiner: Fixed hourly fee per accelerator, plus a data transfer premium layered on normal egress.
trap: DT-Premium is billed on the DOMINANT direction, so an upload-heavy app pays on inbound bytes everyone assumes are free. It is on top of, not instead of, standard EC2 data transfer out.

name: AWS Direct Connect
oneLiner: Port hours run whether or not you push a packet, then per-GB on the way out.
trap: Data transfer IN is free, so people assume the link is cheap, but port hours bill 24/7 while provisioned, and the colo cross-connect is a separate bill from your partner, not AWS.

name: AWS Site-to-Site VPN
oneLiner: Per connection-hour while the tunnel sits in 'available', plus normal egress on what you send.
trap: Billing tracks the available state, not traffic - an idle tunnel still bills. There is no VPN-specific per-GB fee; bytes land on EC2 data transfer out, and the tunnel IPs cost IPv4 hours.

name: AWS Client VPN
oneLiner: Two clocks: one per subnet association running 24/7, one per connected user.
trap: The subnet-association fee bills round the clock with zero users connected, and it is charged per AZ. Each Client VPN ENI also carries an in-use public IPv4 address charge.

name: Public IPv4 Address
oneLiner: Every public IPv4 address costs per hour now, attached or not, on any AWS service.
trap: It is not just EC2 - RDS, ELB, EKS nodes, NAT gateways, VPN tunnels and Global Accelerator all carry it. BYOIP addresses are free and IPv6 is free, which is the whole point of the charge.

name: Elastic IP Address
oneLiner: Since Feb 2024 an EIP costs the same per hour whether it is attached to something or idle.
trap: Hunting down unattached EIPs used to be the whole optimisation; attached ones now bill identically. Both share the PublicIPv4 usage types - use lineItem/Operation to tell them apart.
